name: Work Permit (Çalışma İzni)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a job offer, generally after 6 months' prior residence in Turkey unless exempted, filed by the employer via the e-İzin system.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer and complete the e-İzin application.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the employer to meet the 5:1 rule (at least 5 Turkish citizens per foreign employee), have paid-in capital of at least 500,000 TRY for newly established firms (or 8,000,000 TRY net sales / $150,000 exports for existing firms), unless exempted (firms with ≥50,000,000 TRY annual net sales may employ up to 5 foreigners without the ratio; a foreign partner with capital share ≥$100,000 is exempt from the ratio, capital, and staff rules).
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the employer meets the applicable exemption or ratio requirement.

evidence_required.document: Employer's compliance evidence for the 5:1 ratio or applicable exemption

outcome.duration_length: initial up to 1 year, extendable to 2 then 3 years; also serves as a residence permit

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Social Security — International Labour Force Law No. 6735

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL FINDING: the blocker isn't always the applicant — the 5:1 Turkish-staff ratio and capital/sales thresholds are conditions on the EMPLOYER, similar in spirit to the sponsor-side conditions flagged on several other countries' work routes in this dataset (e.g. Australia's Inländervorrang-style tests), but with a genuinely unusual numeric ratio mechanic (5 Turkish staff per foreign hire) not seen elsewhere in the full research pass. A foreign company partner with a capital share of at least $100,000 is EXEMPT from all three employer-side conditions (ratio, capital, staff count) — a real and consequential carve-out worth surfacing since it effectively creates a faster lane for foreign-invested businesses. A work permit itself also functions as a residence permit — no separate residence application is needed, a genuine administrative simplification distinct from most other countries in this dataset where work authorization and residence permission are separate documents/processes.
